headline_marked: Measles Outbreak: [[Death toll reaches 1,128]] in Bangladesh
headline: Measles Outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,128 in Bangladesh
summary: Three more people died in the last 24 hours as hospital admissions for measles symptoms climb toward 175,000.
details: Three people died with measles symptoms in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Two of these deaths occurred in the Chattogram Division and one in Dhaka.
The combined death toll from measles and measles-like symptoms has reached 1,128 this year. This includes 1,026 deaths with symptoms and 102 confirmed positive cases.
Hospital admissions have surged to 175,336, with 168,142 patients having recovered and returned home.
Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of fatalities, with 466 deaths, followed by Sylhet with 179 and Rajshahi with 93.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,296 people arrived at hospitals with symptoms, and 1,179 of them were admitted.
The DGHS has been tracking these cases since March 15. However, the actual number of cases remains undetermined as not everyone with symptoms is tested or seeks hospital care.
Total people with measles symptoms have reached 197,722, including 21,808 confirmed cases.
caption:
1,128 deaths and nearly 175,000 hospitalizations. Bangladesh is facing a severe measles outbreak.

Three people died with measles symptoms in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Two of these deaths occurred in the Chattogram Division and one in Dhaka.

The combined death toll from measles and measles-like symptoms has reached 1,128 this year. This includes 1,026 deaths with symptoms and 102 confirmed positive cases.

Hospital admissions have surged to 175,336, with 168,142 patients having recovered and returned home.

Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of fatalities, with 466 deaths, followed by Sylhet with 179 and Rajshahi with 93.

In the last 24 hours alone, 1,296 people arrived at hospitals with symptoms, and 1,179 of them were admitted.

The DGHS has been tracking these cases since March 15. However, the actual number of cases remains undetermined as not everyone with symptoms is tested or seeks hospital care.

Total people with measles symptoms have reached 197,722, including 21,808 confirmed cases.
